platformHandling.platform: Major Social Media (Instagram, X, TikTok, Facebook)
platformHandling.detail: Most large platforms compress images and remove EXIF headers to protect user privacy and save server storage.

platformHandling.platform: Direct File Transfer (AirDrop, Bluetooth, USB Drive)
platformHandling.detail: Sharing unmodified raw files sends the 100% untouched byte stream, including GPS coordinates and camera serial numbers.

platformHandling.platform: Cloud Sharing (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox Public Links)
platformHandling.detail: Cloud drives preserve byte-for-byte fidelity, allowing anyone with the download link to inspect EXIF metadata.

platformHandling.status: EXIF Preserved When Sent As File
platformHandling.detail: Standard photos are compressed and stripped, but selecting 'Send as Document/Uncompressed' retains raw metadata.

challengeQuestion.question: Two photos are posted under different anonymous usernames. If both files contain the same camera serial number in their EXIF metadata, what can an investigator reasonably infer?
options: The files may have come from the same camera body, although this alone does not identify who took the photos.
The photos share the same RGB color values in the top-left pixel
Both images have the exact same file size to the byte
The shutter speed proves the person pushed the button with the same finger pressure
challengeQuestion.explanation: Some cameras include a device serial number in manufacturer-specific EXIF MakerNotes. If present and preserved, a matching serial can suggest that two image files came from the same camera body. It does not prove who took either photo, and many devices or sharing platforms omit or remove this information.
challengeQuestion.mitigation: Before sharing an original image, review and remove location and identifying metadata when appropriate. A screenshot may remove some original metadata, but check the resulting file rather than assuming every platform or method strips all identifying information.
